value: The most established enterprise governance platform from a traditional software vendor. Covers model monitoring, drift detection, fairness testing, and audit-trail generation across both IBM and third-party models. Sold to regulated industries on the strength of its on-premises deployment option and IBM's compliance track record.
engine: Monitors models from any provider. Runs its own explainability and fairness algorithms.
latency: Background monitoring, not interactive. Dashboards update periodically.

pricing.includes: Managed deployment, monitoring, and explainability features

quality: Deep and auditable. Configuration complexity is real, and the investment in setup is proportional to the environment it is managing.
tagline: IBM's enterprise AI governance platform: model monitoring, explainability, and audit.
use_cases: Monitoring production ML models for drift, bias, and performance degradation
Generating explainability artifacts for regulator inquiries
Building a governed model lifecycle from training through retirement
integrations: IBM Watson Studio and the wider IBM data and AI stack
Enterprise data warehouses and feature stores
governance_note: This is what an AI audit of a regulated organization's model estate looks like in practice: continuous monitoring, explainability, and documented evidence rather than a point-in-time review. The EU AI Act's high-risk system requirements (Article 9 risk management, Article 17 quality management) describe exactly this kind of ongoing oversight. The product is expensive and complex, and the right question is whether your model estate is large enough to justify it, or whether lighter tooling covers the actual scope.
training_optout: On-premises deployment means model and data stay on your infrastructure. Cloud deployment follows IBM's standard data terms.
